acceptanceCriteriaNotes: LATTICE, DISPROOF FIRST — ROUND 17'S CHANGE DID NOT MAKE IT WORSE, MEASURED THREE INDEPENDENT WAYS. (1) DIRECTIONAL DECOMPOSITION. `detail` is mean |4L - 4 neighbours| = mean |2*hpX + 2*hpY|. Split it: in the target box 2274,377 241x60 the x-direction part is 0.568 (r16v1) -> 0.575 (r17v2), +1.2%, while the y-direction part is 0.738 -> 1.919, x2.60. A vertical lattice lives entirely in the x part. The whole 1.14 -> 2.20 rise is horizontal banding. (2) THE CRITIC'S OWN CONTROL MOVED THE SAME WAY, AND TERRAIN CANNOT DRAW THERE. Box 2274,269 241x60: y-part 0.552 -> 1.340, x-part 0.415 -> 0.367; detail 0.91 -> 1.54, lumaSpread 21.0 -> 35.9. The twin puts zero band coverage at every row of that box. (3) TWIN DECOMPOSITION. Band-correlated share of the column signal in x 2280..2520, y 400..470 is rho * RMS = 0.602 * 0.433 = 0.261 at r16v1 and 0.430 * 0.605 = 0.260 at r17v2 — unchanged to 0.4% — while the band-UNcorrelated share rose 0.345 -> 0.546, +58%. ALSO NOTE: removing 100% of the column-coherent structure from the target box changes its detail by 0.002 (2.201 -> 2.203). The number the critic quoted has never been measuring the lattice.

LATTICE, MECHANISM, FOUND BY ABLATION NOT BY GUESS. The twin was ablated term by term on the shipped r17 slope, measuring the band's own column-signal RMS in the artefact box (baseline 0.9379): kill the gully field 0.9166 (x0.977), the coarse grain 0.9421 (x1.005), the fine grain 0.9377 (x1.000), the massif identity 0.9627, the crest relief 0.9700, the snow 0.9477 — and kill the slope-driven `lit` term 0.5420 (x0.578). `lit` is the comb, and nothing else is within 3%. The reason is that a one-texel difference is a DERIVATIVE, so it multiplies every frequency in the baked profile by that frequency, and the profile carries deliberate high-frequency content: the serration terms at serR 148-232 run at 1-2 deg of arc = 25-50 review px, authored to break the silhouette, not to be lit. That is why the measured period of the comb is 17-25 px and not the band's 4.8 px texel pitch, and it is the 'second, coarser rectilinear source' round 17 filed as a residual.

LATTICE, FIX. kgRidge's slope baseline widened from a +/-1 texel central difference to +/-8 texels, still taken at each end of the span and lerped by the same f the height uses, so it stays C0. Landform-scale slope RMS vs texel-scale residual RMS, rank 2, whole horizon: one-texel 0.603/8.447 (ratio 14.0), r17's +/-1 0.599/5.019 (8.4), +/-8 0.569/1.441 (2.5). The landform signal is held to within 5.6% and `face` over the horizon is unchanged to three decimals (mean 0.483 -> 0.484, sd 0.459 -> 0.459, p5 0.000, p95 1.000), so the bearing-dependent rock lighting that rounds 15-16 added survives intact. 8 texels is 1.41 deg of arc, 38 review px in wide, 123 m of horizon arc at 5 km — a mountain flank rather than a wiggle. Twin-measured band column signal: 1.330 (pre-17) -> 0.938 (r17) -> 0.306. Cost six taps instead of four on a 2048x4 NEAREST texture; +0 draw calls, +0 triangles.

LATTICE, THE SHED GATE, A SILENT SIDE-EFFECT CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED. `shed` reads the same slope, so widening the baseline shrank its argument 3x and the gate stopped biting: the fraction of the horizon with shed < 0.5 fell 0.0273 -> 0.0007, which would have quietly snowed over every steep crest with no error and no log. Sweeping the coefficient: 0.045 -> 0.0007 frac, 0.060 -> 0.0042, 0.080 -> 0.0125, 0.100 -> 0.0210, 0.137 -> 0.0334 but column signal 0.3722, 0.180 -> 0.0496 and 0.4626. 0.100 restores the distribution to 0.0210 against the old 0.0273 at no cost to the column signal (0.3063 against 0.3065). Snow now sheds off a steep flank rather than off an individual 6 m texel.

LATTICE, PREDICTION, WITH THE SHORTFALL DECLARED BEFORE THE SHOT. (a) `probe stats shots/phone-wide-rN.png 0.898,0.322,0.095,0.051` detail: PREDICT NO MEASURABLE MOVE, 2.05-2.25, against an acceptance of <= 1.20. THE ACCEPTANCE WILL NOT BE MET AND IT CANNOT BE MET IN THIS FILE. The arithmetic: that box's detail is 2.20, of which the y-direction part alone is 1.919; deleting every column-coherent pixel changes it by 0.002. Even zeroing 100% of the x-direction structure leaves 1.63. And the criterion's own guard pins the clean-sky control at 1.54 +/- 0.35, i.e. it requires the artefact box to end up SMOOTHER THAN THE SKY DIRECTLY ABOVE IT. (b) lumaSpread <= 24: already 20.6, predict unchanged, PASS. (c) The clause the fix is actually aimed at, 'no straight line longer than 40 px above the mountain silhouette': band column-signal RMS in x 2280..2520, y 400..470 is 0.605 at r17v2 with a band-correlated share of 0.260. The twin puts the band's own contribution at x0.327, so predict the correlated share falls to about 0.085 and the box total to sqrt(0.085^2 + 0.546^2) = 0.553, i.e. PREDICT 0.53-0.58, -8.6%. That is small because the band is no longer the dominant term in that box — which is the disproof above, restated as a number. CONTAMINATION, DECLARED: foliage, postfx and sky are changing the same frame, and the 0.546 uncorrelated part is theirs; the only quantity this owner is the sole plausible mover of is the band-correlated share. (d) GUARDS SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: control box 0.898,0.230 has zero band coverage in the twin at every row <= 378, so nothing here can move it; massif box 0.760,0.322 is opaque clipmap terrain drawn over a renderOrder -20 band, and it measured detail 3.02 -> 3.03 and meanRGB [178.3,156.3,153.1] -> [178.3,156.3,153.1] across a round in which the band changed.

DRESSING, WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE ON THE SHIPPED FRAME. Criterion (1) yaw >= 12 deg and height >= 8%: round 17 measured 34.4-161.7 deg of yaw and 17.7-30.5% of height between every consecutive pair, and nothing this round moves a lantern transform — no shared or private random draw changed, no position changed, Level.js was not opened. PREDICT UNCHANGED AND PASSING. Criterion (3) spacing >= 15%: +/-24% and +/-31% about each row's own mean, unchanged, PASSING. The mechanisms the critic's hypothesis says are missing are all present and were verified in file: per-instance yaw (uniform 0..2pi), per-instance lean (2-5 deg on a third of them, with a sink term so the low corner stays in the dirt), per-instance scale (0.80-1.24 with an anti-clustering fold), a per-instance quarry tint and a per-instance moss tint at a 0.26 rate. The hypothesis 'the placement pass probably emits a fixed transform per slot with no jitter and no variant channel' is DISPROVED IN FILE.

DRESSING, CRITERION (2) — THE ANSWER IS THAT IT CANNOT BE GUARANTEED WITHIN ITS OWN GUARD, AND HERE IS THE ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN THE ARGUMENT. weatherFace is a per-VERTEX colour term, so its finest possible feature is the mesh's circumferential pitch. The lantern shaft is circleProfile(12) — 30 deg per vertex — and the plinth is hexProfile() at 60 deg. The lobe's full-strength core at half * 0.45 = 33.8 deg therefore spanned 2.3 shaft vertices and 1.1 plinth vertices, and the worley rosette field that was supposed to make the lichen read as discrete blotches was being sampled two or three times across the entire patch. At that density it can only ever be a smooth tint ramp. THE PATTERN CANNOT BE BOUGHT: taking the shaft to circleProfile(24) is +600 geometry triangles, and report-r17v2.json records level/lantern:__lanternStone at calls 3, triangles 121,824, instances 24 — i.e. 1,692 per geometry and 72x submitted — so the rollup would charge 3 * 24 * 600 = 43,200 against a 4,000 allocation, 10.8x over. A second prototype or a variant texture is about +5 draw calls on a frame at 119 of 140, and the finding's own guard forbids new draw calls by name. So the criterion as written is not satisfiable as a guarantee; it is a coin flip on the yaw.

DRESSING, WHAT LANDED, AND ITS HONEST SIZE. weatherFace's full-strength inner edge moved half * 0.45 -> half * 0.72, i.e. 33.8 deg -> 54.0 deg. Outer extent and therefore total circumference covered are unchanged; only the solid part widens. At the real sampling that takes the third vertex round the shaft from t 0.280 to t 0.740, so the core goes from 2.3 to 3.6 vertices and the lobe reads as a resolved flank instead of a two-vertex smear. On a cos-weighted projected-area model of the front 180 deg with a uniform yaw, the probability that a given lantern shows >= 15% of its visible area at full contrast rises from 0.208 to 0.338; with the two foreground lanterns the crop actually contains, 0.37 -> 0.56. PREDICT: STILL A COIN FLIP, NOT A PASS, AND IT IS REPORTED AS A SHORTFALL BEFORE THE SHOT. Cost +0 triangles, +0 draw calls: it is one multiplier in a vertex-colour pass.

DRESSING, MEASURED ON THE SHIPPED FRAME so the next owner does not re-derive it. Foreground lanterns in phone-torii-r17v2.png: the left shaft's G/R profile across x 115..193 at y 960..1100 runs 0.647 0.690 0.676 0.710 0.714 0.718 0.722 0.721 0.724 0.719 0.736 0.724 0.727 0.722 — flat-to-rising, i.e. one flank greener than a cylinder should be — while the right shaft at x 495..567, y 985..1125 runs 0.704 0.668 0.651 0.642 0.638 0.629 0.620 0.610 0.610 0.616 0.610 0.630 0.702, the U-shape of plain cylindrical shading. So the lobe IS realised on the left lantern and is absent on the right. Its size is a tint shift of about 11% in G/R, not a blotch. NOTE FOR ANY FUTURE MOSS MEASUREMENT: G > R does not work as a moss test in this scene. Under a sun of colour [1, 0.412, 0.134] every surface in the torii crop is R > G > B, including bamboo foliage (G>R fraction 0.009) and the mossiest lantern face (0.001). Use G/R against the same prop's unweathered stone.

DRESSING, DECLINED, WITH REASONS, so nobody re-opens them blind. (a) RAISING THE LEAN RATE from 0.34. The lean is drawn as `vary() < 0.34 ? 0.035 + vary() * 0.055 : 0.0`, so the BRANCH DECIDES HOW MANY NUMBERS COME OFF THE PRIVATE STREAM, and that same stream is read a few lines later by `rowZ` to set the approach lanterns' Z pitch. Changing the rate — even to a constant two-draw form — reshuffles rowZ and moves every approach lantern, which would invalidate the spacing criterion that currently passes at +/-24%/+/-31%, with no capture available this round to re-verify. (b) STRENGTHENING THE PER-INSTANCE MOSS TINT at its 0.26 rate. This is the exact knob whose previous setting is recorded in Level.js as 'took up to 6% off blue on every single lantern and never added any back ... a large part of why these read as pale sandy clay'. An unverifiable retune of a knob with that history is not worth a minor finding. Both are cheap and both are available to a round that can actually re-shoot.

risks: NOTHING IN THIS ROUND HAS BEEN RENDERED BY THIS OWNER. Every number is a pixel measurement of the r16/r16v1/r17v1/r17v2 frames, or the offline band twin, or a count read off report-r17v2.json. The twin is validated by being able to identify which slope variant each build shipped (correlation diagonal above), but it carries no post-processing and no sky, so it is used only for ratios and correlations.

The +/-8 texel baseline is a judgement about scale, not a tuned constant. If the verification frame shows the far ranges reading FLATTER — faces that no longer separate warm from cool along the horizon — the knob is KG_SLOPE_ARM and 4 is the next stop (twin column signal 0.406 against 0.306, residual ratio 3.9 against 2.5). The measurement that says this is safe is that `face` over the whole horizon is unchanged to three decimals; the measurement that would falsify it is a drop in the massif-to-massif tint spread.

The shed coefficient 0.100 was chosen to hold the shed-fraction distribution, not by looking at snow in a frame. If the far crests read snowier or barer than r17v2, that is where to look, and the sweep is recorded above.
weatherFace's wider core makes 24 lanterns solidly mossy over a wider flank. It is unverified this round. If it reads as a wash rather than a flank, half * 0.60 is the intermediate step.
